items.kind: Present Simple instead of Present Continuous
items.pattern: Present Simple for today/now in contrast with a habit
items.sk: Dnes je to inak, patrí Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.cz: Dnes je to jinak, patří Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.en: Today is different, so Present Continuous: “{right}”.

items.pattern: is/are + -ing with usually/always/every…
items.en: For a habit, use Present Simple: “{right}”.

items.kind: Past Simple instead of Present Continuous
items.pattern: past form for what is happening now/today
items.sk: Deje sa to teraz, patrí Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.cz: Děje se to teď, patří Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.en: It is happening now, so Present Continuous: “{right}”.

items.pattern: drop -s/-es from a he/she/it verb
drop am/is/are before the -ing verb
am/is/are + base verb (is hold)
am knowing, is liking, is wanting, are needing
items.en: Verbs like “know” or “like” take no -ing here: “{right}”.

items.pattern: Present Simple for a temporary situation (She lives with us this month)
items.sk: Je to dočasné, lepšie sedí Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.cz: Je to dočasné, lépe sedí Present Continuous: „{right}“.
items.en: It is temporary, so Present Continuous fits better: “{right}”.

items.pattern: is/are + -ing for a permanent fact (The river is flowing into the sea)
items.sk: Ide o fakt, patrí Present Simple: „{right}“.
items.cz: Jde o fakt, patří Present Simple: „{right}“.
items.en: It is a fact, so Present Simple: “{right}”.

items.pattern: always/usually/often after the verb
am/is/are not matching the subject (they is, he are)
siting, makeing, lieing, runing
don't/doesn't + -ing (She doesn't dancing)
isn't + base verb for a habit (She isn't eat meat)
items.en: For a habit, the negative is “don't/doesn't”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: translate sa/se as himself/herself/itself/you
drop the subject pronoun (SK/CZ pro-drop)
adjective where the -ly adverb is needed (slow for slowly)
items.en: With a verb, use the -ly form: “{right}”.

items.pattern: drop a/an/the before a noun
replace the preposition with a typical SK/CZ calque (in/on/at/to/for)
a different word whose meaning does not fit (carry for wear, listen for hear)
